one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall on the same day inside the window: GEV 3Q26 earnings on 2026-10-28 (IR events page) and the FOMC decision on 2026-10-28. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16, its first hike since 2023, and the median dot (4.1% for end-2026) points to one more (src 21). The 10-year Treasury is at 5.29% and the 30-year at 5.64% (H.15, 9/30, src 22), so a second hike would be another multiple headwind for a ~40x stock. On earnings, orders are largely pre-announced: at Laguna on 9/16 the CEO flagged 'a very strong third quarter orders performance' and a $200B backlog 'very early in 2027', and said most new 2030-31 slots get contracted in 4Q (src 7). The risk is in the P&L. 2Q EPS of $2.47 missed ~$3.04 (src 16), 3Q consensus of ~$4.1 needs a big sequential step (src 20), and 1H Wind EBITDA of -$657M against a ~-$400M FY guide (src 2) means 2H Wind must earn ~+$250M, the line most likely to be re-guided. Positives: 3Q buybacks (1H26 averaged ~$918 a share, src 2), Evercore raised its 2027-28 estimates 3-4% on 10/1, which drove the +3.9% day (src 23), and strong peer gas orders (src 12). Negatives: GLJ's $470 Sell on 9/14 (-8.6% that day, src 13) and the late-September behind-the-meter headlines (src 19). The two same-day events widen the distribution a little but give me no directional edge. I use a lognormal with median ~$983 (a hair below spot for the rate risk) and sigma 15% (annual 52% / 3.5).

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E (2028E EPS ~$30 x 32x = $960, applied in Oct-2027) + 40% normalized FCF yield (2028E FCF $8.0B at 3.4% = ~$235B, + $10.5B net cash with no deposit haircut, / ~262M shares = ~$938). Blend ~$950. That is down from $985: the rates backdrop (Fed hike on 9/16, 10-year at 5.29%) takes off 1x of P/E and 15bp of FCF yield, partly offset by using reported net cash.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E revenue $57B x 19.5% adj EBITDA margin = ~$11.1B; less ~$1.5B D&A (PP&E ~$0.9B + intangibles ~$0.6B); less ~$0.2B excluded items; plus ~$0.35B net interest; 21% tax -> ~$7.7B net income / ~262M diluted shares = ~$29.4. Blended with consensus 2028E ~$30.5 -> $30; x 32x

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's 2028 outlook is $56B including Prolec (4Q25 release). I add ~$1B because the CEO at Laguna expects 2028 Prolec financials to be 'materially better' than projected, and 2026 revenue guidance went from $44-45B (Jan) to $45.5-46.5B (Jul).
Management targets 20% (Power 22%, Electrification 22%, Wind 6%). I trim 0.5pt for execution: 1H26 margin was 10.5% vs the 12-14% FY guide, and Wind lost $657M in 1H26 (10-Q segment note).

inputs_detail.value: Revenue $45.5-46.5B; adj EBITDA margin 12-14%; FCF $11.5-12.5B; Wind ~-$400M EBITDA

inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q 1H26: PP&E depreciation $348M and intangible amortization $411M (up from $116M after the Prolec step-up), ~ $1.5B annualized. I hold ~$1.5B for 2028: PP&E depreciation rises with capex ($783M in 1H26) while purchase intangibles amortize down. Round 1 used ~$1.2B.

271M diluted weighted shares in 1H26 and 266.3M outstanding at Jun-30. $3B is left on the $10B authorization, and the CEO said 3Q26 gave 'another good opportunity' to buy. Net ~1.5% a year of reduction.

The 1H26 ETR of 10.5% is distorted by the nontaxable $3.99B Prolec remeasurement gain. The 2Q26 ETR was 29.8%, inflated by purchase-price-allocation updates and losses with no tax benefit. 1H25 was 22.6%. I normalize to ~21%.

Cross-check only. Evercore raised its 2027-28 estimates 3-4% on 10/1 and sits 2-7% above consensus (src 23). My bottom-up $29.4 is close to consensus, so I keep $30 rather than chase the raise before 3Q prints.

Spot is ~33x my 2028E and ~40-44x consensus 2027E. In Oct-2027, 2028 is the one-year-forward year, so the multiple compresses as EPS growth slows from ~40% toward ~20-25%. Round 2 trims 33x to 32x for rates. The FOMC hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 with one more hike signalled (src 21). The 10-year is 5.29% (src 22), so a 33x earnings yield of 3.0% sits ~2.3pt below the risk-free rate. Spot already prices most of that, so I take only 1x off. What supports a premium: 2030 is mostly sold out and 2032 slots are selling with cash down (src 7), and peer Siemens Energy has rising gas-services margins (src 12). What caps it: GLJ's 2030-31 overcapacity case (src 13, 15).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Normalized 2028E FCF $8.0B / 3.4% = ~$235B; + $10.5B net cash (reported $10.3B at Jun-30 rolled to YE26, no deposit haircut because deposits are already in the lower FCF) = ~$246B; / 262M shares = ~$938

inputs_detail.derivation: FY25 was $3.7B. With ~$12B in 2026, the target implies only >= ~$8B across 2027-28. It was set before the 2026 raise, so it is conservative, but it signals deposits partly normalizing.

~$7.7B net income + ~$1.5B D&A - ~$1.6B capex (1H26 annualized and rising) ~ $7.6B. I round up to $8.0B for continued modest deposit build: the CEO says the progress balance still grows more slowly than margin in backlog. Round 1 used $9.0B. I cut it because contract liabilities have already risen $14.1B in 1H26 to $39.9B, and the guide implies only ~$1.6-2.6B of 2H26 FCF.

Reported: $13.12B cash less $2.85B total borrowings ($2.79B long-term notes plus other) = $10.3B at Jun-30 (10-Q, src 2). For YE26 I add ~$2B of 2H26 FCF (implied by the FY guide, src 1) and subtract 3Q-4Q buybacks and dividends (~$1.8B), which gives ~$10.5B. Round 1 cut this to ~$8B for customer deposits. As the supervisor noted, that double-counted the deposit unwind, which my $8.0B normalized FCF (vs $11.5-12.5B 2026) already reflects. I now haircut FCF only.

This sits between a premium electrical-equipment compounder (~3%) and a cyclical capital-goods discount (~4%+, the GLJ view). I raised it from 3.25% because the 10-year is now 5.29% (src 22) after the 9/16 hike. A growth-adjusted FCF yield this far below the risk-free rate needs ~6%+ long-run FCF growth, which the backlog supports, but with less room than in round 1.

bear.story: AI capex or data-center pushback (state moratoria, behind-the-meter smaller turbines) slows slot conversion. Wind misses its 2H recovery. Another Fed hike keeps the 10-year above 5%. The market adopts GLJ's 2030-31 overcapacity frame and de-rates GEV to ~22x on ~$27 2028E EPS.

base.story: 3Q/4Q orders are strong and the backlog crosses $200B in early 2027. The January call shows a 2026 Power margin-in-backlog change larger than 2025's. The 2026 guide is met and 2028 is reaffirmed or nudged up. The stock trades ~33x a ~$30 2028E, and rates hold it below its 1H26 multiple.

bull.story: The spring-2027 Capital Markets Day sets a 2030 framework well above the 2028 bridge: 30 GW/yr gas output, Electrification above $20B, Wind profitable. 2028E EPS moves to ~$35-36. The market pays ~39x, capped below 40x by higher rates.

thesis_break_reason: ~$640 (35% below spot, ~21x my $30 2028E EPS) is consistent only with a broken 2028 outlook: slot reservations not converting to orders, margin in backlog going flat (Siemens or Mitsubishi capacity hitting price), or a material AI/data-center capex retrenchment. I checked whether rates alone could get there. With the 10-year already at 5.29% and spot near 33x 2028E, one more 25bp hike would plausibly cost a few turns, not twelve, so $640 still needs a fundamental break. My ladder puts ~17% probability below it, mostly from the bear branch.

key_uncertainties: Durability of AI and data-center power demand and the cyclical case against it. The 9/14 -8.6% day coincided with GLJ's $470 Sell initiation, while Eaton fell 7% and Quanta 4% on the AI-slowdown theme. State moratoria are live (NY enacted; Polymarket 18% for another state by year-end).

Rates: the Fed restarted hiking on 9/16 (3.75-4.00%) with one more hike signalled, and the 10-year is at 5.29% and the 30-year at 5.64%, the highest since 2002. For a stock at ~40x 2027E, the discount rate is a live multiple risk.

Whether gas turbine demand is secular or cyclical: GLJ sees 104-113 GW of 2030-31 capacity vs 88-90 GW of demand. Against that, 2032 slots are selling with cash down, and Siemens and Mitsubishi are both expanding capacity.
Margin ramp and EPS quality: 1H26 adj EBITDA margin was 10.5% vs the 12-14% guide, 2Q EPS missed, and post-Prolec amortization is ~$0.8B a year.
Wind: the 1H26 loss of $657M means 2H must earn ~+$250M to hit the ~-$400M guide; US onshore orders remain soft and Section 232 tariff clarity is pending.
FCF normalization: $39.9B of contract liabilities. 2026 FCF is deposit-driven, and the >= $24B 2025-28 cumulative target implies modest 2027-28 FCF.
CFO transition during a peak-execution period (Parks retiring; McDonough CFO from 2027-01-01).
reasoning: Round 2 starts from my round-1 primary-document work (10-Q, 2Q call and Laguna transcripts, 8-Ks, investor updates). The supervisor confirmed my catalyst calendar and found three things I missed. (1) Net cash: I had cut it to ~$8B for deposits on top of cutting normalized FCF to $8.0B, which double-counts. I re-read the 10-Q (cash $13.12B, borrowings $2.85B, net $10.3B) and now haircut only FCF, using ~$10.5B at YE26, worth about +$9/share. (2) Rates: I verified the 9/16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (Fed release) and found the 10-year at 5.29% and the 30-year at 5.64% on 9/30 (H.15), which is more than the supervisor's fed-funds framing captured. I take 1x off the forward P/E (33x to 32x) and raise the FCF yield 15bp (3.25% to 3.4%), about -$30 and -$40/share on those legs. (3) The 9/14 drop coincided with GLJ's Sell initiation; I've corrected that. New evidence: Evercore raised its 2027-28 estimates 3-4% on 10/1. That is mildly positive for revisions, but I keep my bottom-up $30 2028E EPS until 3Q prints. September company releases (a 96 MW Scotland onshore order, Egypt 9F life-extension services) are small and do not change the Wind or Power numbers. Fair value is $950 (P/E $960 x 0.6, FCF yield $938 x 0.4), down from $985 and below the supervisor's reconciled $1,005. I disagree with that figure because it carries no rate adjustment and its EPS range ($30-32) sits above my post-Prolec D&A and tax build. The scenarios (25% $600 / 50% $1,000 / 25% $1,400) have a mean of ~$1,000. Ladder: 85% lognormal (median $1,015, sigma 0.40) plus 15% bear-branch lognormal (median $680, sigma 0.45). The overall median is ~$965, P(>=987) is 0.48 and the mean is ~$1,045. Dispersion stays ~43%, below the 52% realized but well above the large-cap base rate. The median sits between fair value and the scenario mean because estimate momentum (Evercore, the 3Q orders pre-signal) argues against centring fully on my lower fair value. Lane note: round 2 added two Fed macro sources (not lane-type but needed to act on the supervisor's rates finding), one sell-side note and two company releases. In-lane share is ~56%, slightly under the 60% target, because the rate check had no primary-company equivalent. Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were not used. CNBC returned 403, so yields come from the Fed's own H.15.
